content.NASA POWER · latest available · GEOS-IT: NASA POWER · latest available · GEOS-IT + MERRA-2 · ZXQPHRASE0QXZ
content.Daily NASA POWER precipitation from MERR: Daily NASA POWER precipitation from MERRA-2, extended with the GEOS-IT near-real-time analysis. Recent values are model estimates, typically about two days behind.
content.Rainfall becomes a patter of drops and s: Rainfall becomes a patter of drops and soft water noise.
content.Daily NASA POWER 10-meter wind from MERR: Daily NASA POWER 10-meter wind from MERRA-2, extended with the GEOS-IT near-real-time analysis. The global wind map uses a separate NASA MERRA-2 monthly raster.
content.Wind speed shapes the pitch and swell of: Wind speed shapes the pitch and swell of an airy whoosh.
content.Daily NASA POWER precipitation and 10-me: Daily NASA POWER precipitation and 10-meter wind from MERRA-2, extended with GEOS-IT near real time. Current values are model analyses, not storm warnings.
content.Satellite rain makes the patter; stronge: Satellite rain makes the patter; stronger wind swells the low roar.
content.ZXQPHRASE0QXZ mm of estimated rain per d: ZXQPHRASE0QXZ mm of estimated rain per day. More rain adds faster, brighter drops.
content.ZXQPHRASE0QXZ m/s at 10 meters. Stronger: ZXQPHRASE0QXZ m/s at 10 meters. Stronger wind deepens the moving air sound.
content.ZXQPHRASE0QXZ mm/day of satellite-estima: ZXQPHRASE0QXZ mm/day of satellite-estimated rain, layered with local 10-meter wind.
content.NASA GISS global land-ocean temperature: NASA GISS global land-ocean temperature anomaly relative to 1951–1980. GISTEMP is a NASA analysis using documented NOAA/NCEI station and sea-surface-temperature inputs. Completed years use annual means; the current year uses the mean of available monthly records to date.
content.Below the 1951–1980 baseline, slow ice c: Below the 1951–1980 baseline, slow ice cracks emerge; above it, a campfire fades in and grows fuller as the anomaly rises.
content.NASA/JPL MUR is a daily, multi-mission s: NASA/JPL MUR is a daily, multi-mission sea-surface temperature analysis. The latest value is the mean of available monthly NASA map samples at the selected ocean point; land and masked pixels stay unavailable.
content.Sea-surface temperature shifts the under: Sea-surface temperature shifts the underwater tone from deep and cool to bright and warm.
content.NASA OCO-2 satellite retrievals of atmos: NASA OCO-2 satellite retrievals of atmospheric column CO₂. The latest value is an approximate mean of sampled valid orbital-swath color bins, not a complete global field.
content.The latest complete NASA Terra MODIS 8-d: The latest complete NASA Terra MODIS 8-day Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) composite. Cloud, water, and masked pixels have no reading.
content.NASA Terra MODIS NDVI · NASA GIBS: NASA Terra MODIS NDVI · NASA GIBS
content.More vegetation adds a wider, fuller cho: More vegetation adds a wider, fuller chord; sparse green cover leaves a simpler note.
content.NASA MODIS 8-day daytime land-surface te: NASA MODIS 8-day daytime land-surface temperature, sampled at the pin from a quality-screened 1 km NASA product pixel. The reading is the surface skin temperature, not the air temperature. Microsoft Planetary Computer distributes the NASA LP DAAC GeoTIFF.
content.NASA MODIS MOD11A2 v061 · Microsoft Plan: NASA MODIS MOD11A2 v061 · Microsoft Planetary Computer
content.Below 0 °C brings in ice cracks; above f: Below 0 °C brings in ice cracks; above freezing, real MODIS surface warmth turns up the campfire crackle.
content.NASA MODIS 8-day Gap-Filled Gross Primar: NASA MODIS 8-day Gap-Filled Gross Primary Productivity (MOD17A2HGF v061). A quality-screened 500 m pixel is sampled at the pin from a NASA LP DAAC cloud-optimized GeoTIFF served through Microsoft Planetary Computer.
content.NASA MODIS MOD17A2HGF v061 · Microsoft P: NASA MODIS MOD17A2HGF v061 · Microsoft Planetary Computer
content.Higher 8-day plant carbon uptake adds mo: Higher 8-day plant carbon uptake adds more notes and a brighter, fuller chord; the sound reaches its full range at 0.4 kg C/m²/8d while displayed NASA values stay uncapped.
content.NASA MODIS daily snow-cover percentage (: NASA MODIS daily snow-cover percentage (MOD10A1 v061), read at the pin from the latest available quality-screened 500 m NASA LP DAAC GeoTIFF served through Microsoft Planetary Computer.
content.NASA MODIS MOD10A1 v061 · Microsoft Plan: NASA MODIS MOD10A1 v061 · Microsoft Planetary Computer
content.The ice-crackle texture becomes denser a: The ice-crackle texture becomes denser as the NASA snow-cover reading rises; zero cover leaves it quiet.
content.Daily relative humidity at 2 meters from: Daily relative humidity at 2 meters from NASA POWER. NASA derives this MERRA-2 estimate from air temperature, specific humidity, and pressure on the model grid; it is not a local weather-station observation.
content.Humidity softens the tone and adds a sub: Humidity softens the tone and adds a subtle watery shimmer as the NASA value rises.
content.Daily specific humidity at 2 meters from: Daily specific humidity at 2 meters from NASA POWER MERRA-2 and its near-real-time GEOS-IT extension. This is water-vapor mass per mass of moist air on a model grid; it is not relative humidity or a surface-water measurement.
content.More water vapor adds a soft, bright syn: More water vapor adds a soft, bright synthesized shimmer; this is not a rain recording.
content.Daily NASA POWER precipitable water: the: Daily NASA POWER precipitable water: the equivalent depth of water if vapor throughout the atmospheric column were condensed. Available from 2001 in this series; it describes column moisture, not rainfall at the surface.
content.More water vapor integrated through the: More water vapor integrated through the atmosphere adds gentle, synthesized watery harmonics; it never plays the measured-rain sample.
content.Daily mean cloud amount from NASA CERES: Daily mean cloud amount from NASA CERES SYN1deg through NASA POWER. The globally gridded estimate combines CERES measurements with cloud properties from MODIS and geostationary imagers; it is not a point sky-camera reading.
content.More cloud cover adds a softer, fuller a: More cloud cover adds a softer, fuller airy layer while the pitch tracks the measured percentage.
content.Daily all-sky shortwave radiation reachi: Daily all-sky shortwave radiation reaching the surface in megajoules per square meter per day. NASA POWER combines the NASA GEWEX SRB record (1984–2000) with NASA CERES products from 2001 onward; clouds are included in the all-sky value.
content.More incoming sunlight brightens the cho: More incoming sunlight brightens the chord and brings in higher, clearer harmonics.
content.Daily all-sky downward longwave radiatio: Daily all-sky downward longwave radiation reaching the surface in megajoules per square meter per day. NASA POWER uses NASA CERES SYN1deg for the climate-quality series from 2001 and CERES FLASHFlux for near-real-time updates; this is energy flux, not air temperature.
content.More downward longwave energy adds gentl: More downward longwave energy adds gentle synthesized harmonics to a low tone; no fire recording is used.
content.NASA CERES SYN1deg adjusted aerosol opti: NASA CERES SYN1deg adjusted aerosol optical depth at 550 nm, distributed by NASA POWER. It describes how aerosols in the full atmospheric column affect light; it is not a direct surface pollution or health measurement.
content.As optical depth rises, the sound become: As optical depth rises, the sound becomes more filtered and subdued, like light passing through a hazier column.
content.Daily mean surface pressure from NASA PO: Daily mean surface pressure from NASA POWER MERRA-2 and its near-real-time GEOS-IT extension. These are gridded model-analysis values, so elevation and the size of the source grid cell matter.
content.Surface pressure anchors a low, steady n: Surface pressure anchors a low, steady note; changes in the NASA reading shift its pitch.
content.Daily 2-meter air temperature from NASA: Daily 2-meter air temperature from NASA POWER MERRA-2 and its near-real-time GEOS-IT extension. This is a gridded analysis estimate at the selected point, not a thermometer or the global GISTEMP anomaly.
content.Below 0 °C brings in ice cracks; as loca: Below 0 °C brings in ice cracks; as local air temperature rises above freezing, a real campfire recording fades in and grows.
content.Daily UTC minimum 2-meter air temperatur: Daily UTC minimum 2-meter air temperature from NASA POWER MERRA-2 and its near-real-time GEOS-IT extension. The daily minimum comes from hourly model temperatures; it is not a station observation.
content.Nighttime lows below freezing add sharpe: Nighttime lows below freezing add sharper ice cracks; warmer lows let the campfire grow.
content.Daily UTC maximum 2-meter air temperatur: Daily UTC maximum 2-meter air temperature from NASA POWER MERRA-2 and its near-real-time GEOS-IT extension. The daily maximum comes from hourly model temperatures; it is not a station observation.
content.Below-freezing highs make sparse ice cra: Below-freezing highs make sparse ice cracks; hotter daily highs bring a fuller, brighter campfire.
content.Daily 2-meter temperature range from NAS: Daily 2-meter temperature range from NASA POWER MERRA-2: the difference between the daily high and low, in degrees Celsius. It is not daily mean temperature or a temperature anomaly.
content.A smaller high-to-low swing keeps a cent: A smaller high-to-low swing keeps a centered note; a wider daily range adds brighter harmonics, without implying a warmer daily mean.
content.Daily wet-bulb temperature at 2 meters f: Daily wet-bulb temperature at 2 meters from NASA POWER MERRA-2 and its near-real-time GEOS-IT extension. It combines temperature and moisture in an atmospheric analysis; it is not a heat-stress alert or a local sensor reading.
content.Below-freezing wet-bulb values add fine: Below-freezing wet-bulb values add fine ice cracks; warmer values bring in a fire texture that grows with the reading.
content.Daily dew/frost point at 2 meters from N: Daily dew/frost point at 2 meters from NASA POWER MERRA-2, with a GEOS-IT near-real-time extension. It describes the temperature at which air reaches saturation; it is a gridded analysis, not a direct fog or surface-moisture observation.
content.Subfreezing dew points bring in fine ice: Subfreezing dew points bring in fine ice cracks; higher dew points add a soft, watery shimmer.
content.Daily surface soil wetness fraction from: Daily surface soil wetness fraction from NASA POWER MERRA-2. This modeled land-surface state is not a direct soil probe or the higher-resolution SMAP soil-moisture product; ocean and some land cells can have no valid value.
content.Wetter soil adds a soft, watery synthesi: Wetter soil adds a soft, watery synthesized shimmer; no rain recording is played for this land-surface estimate.
content.Daily land evaporation from NASA POWER M: Daily land evaporation from NASA POWER MERRA-2, expressed as millimeters of water per day. This gridded model estimate is a land flux, not rain and not a direct measurement from a local station.
content.More modeled evaporation raises and brig: More modeled evaporation raises and brightens the synthesized tone; the sound does not use the rain sample.
content.NASA POWER MERRA-2 daily evapotranspirat: NASA POWER MERRA-2 daily evapotranspiration energy flux associated with plant transpiration. The value is latent-heat energy per area, not millimeters of water or a direct plant-growth measurement.
content.Higher transpiration energy flux adds br: Higher transpiration energy flux adds brighter synthesized harmonics; it does not trigger an unmeasured plant sound.
content.Daily mean 2-meter wind speed from NASA: Daily mean 2-meter wind speed from NASA POWER MERRA-2. This is a gridded near-surface estimate, separate from the existing 10-meter weather series and its wind map layer.
content.The recorded wind ambience grows louder: The recorded wind ambience grows louder and more gusty as the NASA 2-meter wind speed rises.
content.ZXQPHRASE0QXZZXQPHRASE1QXZ °C vs. 1951–1: ZXQPHRASE0QXZZXQPHRASE1QXZ °C vs. 1951–1980. Fire and ice are sound metaphors for a global anomaly, not a local freezing-temperature reading.

content.ZXQPHRASE0QXZ ppm approximate mean of sa: ZXQPHRASE0QXZ ppm approximate mean of sampled NASA OCO-2 total-column swath pixels.
content.NDVI ZXQPHRASE0QXZ from the latest avail: NDVI ZXQPHRASE0QXZ from the latest available NASA Terra MODIS composite. Higher values indicate denser green vegetation.
content.NASA MODIS daytime land-surface temperat: NASA MODIS daytime land-surface temperature: ZXQPHRASE0QXZ °C from the latest available 8-day composite. Cloud and low-quality pixels are skipped.
content.ZXQPHRASE0QXZ kg C/m² over 8 days from t: ZXQPHRASE0QXZ kg C/m² over 8 days from the NASA MODIS GPP pixel. Urban, water, barren, snow, and invalid fill values remain unavailable.
content.ZXQPHRASE0QXZ% snow cover from the lates: ZXQPHRASE0QXZ% snow cover from the latest available quality-screened NASA MODIS daily pixel. Fill, water, cloud, and low-quality values are not treated as readings.

content.ZXQPHRASE0QXZ% daily mean cloud amount f: ZXQPHRASE0QXZ% daily mean cloud amount from NASA CERES SYN1deg distributed by POWER.
content.ZXQPHRASE0QXZ MJ/m²/day of all-sky short: ZXQPHRASE0QXZ MJ/m²/day of all-sky shortwave radiation reaching the surface in the NASA POWER series.
content.ZXQPHRASE0QXZ MJ/m²/day of daily downwar: ZXQPHRASE0QXZ MJ/m²/day of daily downward longwave radiation at the surface from NASA POWER.
content.Aerosol optical depth ZXQPHRASE0QXZ at 5: Aerosol optical depth ZXQPHRASE0QXZ at 550 nm from NASA CERES SYN1deg via POWER; this column value is not surface air quality.
content.ZXQPHRASE0QXZ kPa daily mean surface pre: ZXQPHRASE0QXZ kPa daily mean surface pressure from NASA POWER MERRA-2 / GEOS-IT.

content.ZXQPHRASE0QXZ MJ/m²/day NASA POWER trans: ZXQPHRASE0QXZ MJ/m²/day NASA POWER transpiration energy flux from the MERRA-2 land model.
content.ZXQPHRASE0QXZ m/s daily mean 2-meter win: ZXQPHRASE0QXZ m/s daily mean 2-meter wind speed from NASA POWER MERRA-2.

content.The colder the daily minimum, the more f: The colder the daily minimum, the more frequent and sharper the ice cracks.

content.As the high rises, the fire sample grows: As the high rises, the fire sample grows louder and fuller.

content.Colder wet-bulb temperatures make the ic: Colder wet-bulb temperatures make the ice cracks sharper and more frequent.
content.As wet-bulb temperature rises, a real fi: As wet-bulb temperature rises, a real fire recording fades in and grows.
content.Subfreezing dew/frost points add fine, s: Subfreezing dew/frost points add fine, sharper ice cracks.
content.Higher dew points add a soft synthesized: Higher dew points add a soft synthesized shimmer; it is not a measured rain sound.
content.Lower NASA POWER surface wetness leaves: Lower NASA POWER surface wetness leaves a lighter, drier synthesized sound.
content.A higher wetness fraction adds gentle sy: A higher wetness fraction adds gentle synthesized harmonics; no rain sample is used.
content.Less modeled water loss keeps the sound: Less modeled water loss keeps the sound subdued.

content.Less latent-heat energy from plant trans: Less latent-heat energy from plant transpiration keeps the chord simple.
content.A stronger modeled flux adds upper notes: A stronger modeled flux adds upper notes, not a measured plant sound.
